method: A = 3+ knowledge bases or a won debate, and fits our style. B = fits and needs no missing data. C = needs a missing feature or data feed. D = style conflict. Keyword and scope heuristics; research input only.
note: Advisory only. Nothing here changes live order engines. Hard gates need an owner pick.

rules.title: Be selective; not trading is valid
rules.rule: Take only a few high-quality setups, avoid overtrading, and accept no-trade days; knowing when not to trade preserves capital.

rules.title: Dealer gamma regime: mean-revert vs trend
rules.rule: In positive gamma, fade moves and trade reversion between gamma levels; in negative gamma, expect amplified trending moves and trade with momentum.

rules.title: Define exits and risk before entry
rules.rule: Before every trade, define and record the max loss, stop, targets and position size, and confirm the account can absorb the loss.

rules.title: Enter on retest of broken level
rules.rule: After a level or value edge breaks, enter on the pullback or retest of that level, with targets at the next level.

rules.title: Scale out at first target, protect runner
rules.rule: Take partial profits (often ~50%) at the first target, move the stop on the remainder to breakeven, and let a runner work.

rules.title: Wait for reaction at the level
rules.rule: A level, zone or gamma wall is not an entry by itself; wait for price to reach it and react or reclaim with confirmation before entering.

rules.title: Don't let emotions drive trades
rules.rule: Follow your plan objectively and do not let fear, greed, FOMO or the need to be right drive trading decisions.

rules.title: Fade failed breaks that reclaim
rules.rule: When price pokes beyond a level or value edge, fails to hold and reclaims it, fade back toward the other side of value.

rules.title: Exit when traded level is invalidated
rules.rule: Exit immediately when price accepts through the level or structure that justified the trade, rather than waiting for the full stop.

rules.title: No martingale or revenge trading
rules.rule: Never increase size or re-enter to win back losses; after a loss, stick to the plan or stop.

rules.title: Volatility-scaled stops and targets
rules.rule: Size stop width, and targets, to current volatility (ATR multiples, IV, VIX) and regime rather than using fixed points.

rules.title: Breakouts need acceptance
rules.rule: Treat a breakout as valid only when price shows acceptance and progress beyond the level; failed or unaccepted breakouts imply rotation back into range.

rules.title: Keep strategies and tools simple
rules.rule: Prefer simple strategies and a few core tools, removing extra indicators and complexity as noise and fragility.

rules.title: Short strikes beyond support/resistance
rules.rule: Place short put or credit-spread strikes at or beyond a support/resistance level expected to hold.

rules.title: Trade only liquid instruments
rules.rule: Check volume, open interest and bid/ask spreads before trading, and avoid illiquid instruments with wide spreads.

rules.title: VIX 20 as regime line
rules.rule: Treat VIX below 20 as calm or risk-on and above 20 as fear, chop or de-risking, with readings above roughly 30-35 as extreme.

rules.title: Size by dollar risk / stop distance
rules.rule: Set contract count as the fixed dollar risk divided by the stop distance (plus costs), so every trade risks the same amount.

rules.title: Require candle close beyond level
rules.rule: Confirm a level or pattern break only after a candle closes beyond the boundary, not on intraday wicks.

rules.title: Distrust optimizer best-fit parameters
rules.rule: Treat optimized parameters as curve-fit historical bests: prefer robust parameter regions and validate before trading.

rules.title: Crowded positioning is vulnerable
rules.rule: Treat extreme one-sided or consensus positioning, long or short, as a crowded trade vulnerable to sharp reversals and squeezes.

rules.title: Edges decay with popularity
rules.rule: Expect edges to decay as they become popular or markets become more efficient, and keep searching for new ones.

rules.title: Judge performance risk-adjusted
rules.rule: Evaluate performance by risk-adjusted, durable returns relative to drawdown, not by raw P&L.

rules.title: Add only on confirmation or reduced risk
rules.rule: Add to a position only on predefined confirmation, after moving the existing stop to breakeven or reassessing risk.

rules.title: Aim for modest consistent returns
rules.rule: Target consistent modest returns instead of chasing big wins or making up lost time with speculation.

rules.title: Define complete, objective rules
rules.rule: Specify entry, exit, sizing and execution objectively enough that another person could execute the plan.

rules.title: Location over trigger
rules.rule: Prioritize trade location over entry technique: trade only at clear locations such as value edges and never in the middle of balance.

rules.title: Major moving averages as trend filter
rules.rule: Use the 50/200-day moving averages as the trend reference, and take bullish positions only when price is above them.

rules.title: Position sizing is the core skill
rules.rule: Treat position sizing as the core of risk management; big losses come from oversizing.

rules.title: Stop hunting is a myth
rules.rule: Ignore stop-hunting narratives in deep markets and focus on price, volume and hedging flows.

rules.title: Stops slip; plan for it
rules.rule: Expect stop orders to fill with slippage or gap through, so do not treat the stop as your exact max loss.

rules.title: Target next structural level
rules.rule: Set profit targets at the next mapped structural level, such as daily highs/lows, value-area edges or liquidity.

rules.title: Run uncorrelated strategies for all regimes
rules.rule: Run several uncorrelated strategies, such as trend-following and mean-reversion, so every environment is covered and no single strategy's slump is fatal.

rules.title: Trim after overbought rallies
rules.rule: After large overbought run-ups, trim or protect leveraged and extended positions and expect a pullback or consolidation.

rules.title: Account for trading costs
rules.rule: Include commissions, spreads and slippage in research, since costs can exhaust small edges.

rules.title: Avoid outright shorts
rules.rule: Avoid outright short positions, including SPX shorts, which carry poor hit rates or unlimited risk; express bearish views with capped-risk options instead.

rules.title: Don't sell premium across earnings/news
rules.rule: Filter out premium-selling signals when jump risk such as earnings or major news is present, and sell premium in calmer periods instead.

rules.title: No tips; do your own research
rules.rule: Never trade on social-media tips or others' callouts; treat them only as a starting point for your own due diligence.

rules.title: Size inversely to volatility
rules.rule: Trade smaller in more volatile assets or stressed regimes, using volatility targeting.

rules.title: Compression precedes big moves
rules.rule: Treat volatility or range compression as a precursor to a big move, and enter as price expands away.

rules.title: Define trend by swing structure
rules.rule: Define the trend by higher highs and higher lows (or the reverse) per timeframe, and treat it as intact while the defining swing holds with acceptance.

rules.title: Detect regime, deploy matching model
rules.rule: Explicitly detect the current regime, testing models live if needed, and deploy the strategy that fits it.

rules.title: Exit long options well before expiry
rules.rule: Exit long options and debit spreads well before expiration (for example 10+ sessions or midweek for weeklies) to avoid accelerating theta.

rules.title: Exit on fundamental thesis failure
rules.rule: Exit and accept the loss when fundamentals or physical supply/demand no longer support the position.

rules.title: Gamma walls as support/resistance
rules.rule: Treat the call wall and large positive gamma strikes as resistance/magnets and the put wall as support for intraday direction.

rules.title: Keep independent income while trading
rules.rule: Maintain a stable outside income so trading losses never threaten your livelihood.

rules.title: Liquidity drives equities
rules.rule: Treat global and central-bank liquidity as the master driver, leading equities by months: injections support risk, withdrawal weighs on it.

rules.title: Match method to your personality
rules.rule: Choose or adapt a trading style that fits your own character instead of copying someone else's.

rules.title: Move stop to breakeven at trigger
rules.rule: Move the stop to breakeven once a defined trigger is hit, such as open profit equal to initial risk or price reaching a key gamma/call-wall level.

rules.title: Process over single outcomes
rules.rule: Judge decisions by process across a large sample, not by single outcomes or streaks.

rules.title: Reduce on major moving-average break
rules.rule: Reduce or reassess exposure when price breaks key trend moving averages (50/200-day or 50-week) or relative strength breaks.

rules.title: Rotate to trending, volatile markets
rules.rule: Choose or rotate into whichever market currently has strong volatility and a durable trend.

rules.title: Verify claims before trusting
rules.rule: Examine the evidence for an idea and test it before trusting gurus or magic levels.

rules.title: Very high win rates are unrealistic
rules.rule: Do not expect or trust very high win rates; they are not sustainable across market conditions.

rules.title: Sell only strikes you'd own
rules.rule: Sell cash-secured puts, put spreads and covered calls only on quality stocks at strikes where you would be happy to be assigned.

rules.title: Close-based stops, not single pierce
rules.rule: Trigger exits on closes beyond a structural level or indicator, not on a single intraday pierce.

rules.title: Event IV builds then crushes
rules.rule: Expect implied volatility to build before CPI, FOMC, NFP and OPEX and to be crushed afterward, and factor the crush into event trades.

rules.title: Expected move from IV/16
rules.rule: Estimate the daily expected move as IV (or VIX) divided by 16, scaled by the square root of trading days.

rules.title: High-delta long-dated calls for stock replacement
rules.rule: Use deep ITM, roughly 95-delta, longer-dated calls for stock replacement and PMCC long legs.

rules.title: Hold core conservative allocation
rules.rule: Hold a core allocation to stable assets, sized by time horizon or age.

rules.title: Hypothesis-driven research pipeline
rules.rule: Start from a falsifiable hypothesis and follow a structured research pipeline; use coding tools only to speed testing.

rules.title: Limit session time; stop after early trade
rules.rule: Limit discretionary trading to a short early window and stop for the day after the first trade or profit, because decision quality declines.

rules.title: Pre-map zones and wait
rules.rule: Mark zones in advance and trade only when price reaches a pre-mapped level.

rules.title: Psychology dominates trading success
rules.rule: Treat personality and inner psychology as major determinants of trading success.

rules.title: Size so total premium loss is acceptable
rules.rule: Size option positions on the maximum possible loss, so that losing the entire premium is tolerable.

rules.title: Wait for consolidation after extended move
rules.rule: After an extended or overbought move, stand aside until consolidation forms a new setup.

rules.title: Widening credit spreads warn of risk
rules.rule: Monitor high-yield credit spreads; widening is a leading recession and risk signal that warrants hedging or reducing risk.

rules.title: Anti-martingale: scale up only with profits
rules.rule: Increase size only with profits or documented consistency, and remove added size when the edge weakens.

rules.title: Bond volatility speed hits equities
rules.rule: Watch the speed of bond volatility (MOVE, 10Y momentum), because rapid spikes drive equity declines.

rules.title: Cap total options exposure
rules.rule: Cap total options exposure and short-premium collateral as a share of the portfolio.

rules.title: Compare implied vs realized volatility
rules.rule: Judge option premium richness by comparing implied volatility with realized or historical volatility.

rules.title: Credit spread payoff mechanics
rules.rule: Treat a credit spread as a defined-risk trade where max profit is the net credit and max loss is the width minus the credit.

rules.title: Divergence needs confirmation
rules.rule: Use RSI or CVD divergence as an early warning only, never as a standalone trade.

rules.title: Don't chase beyond entry band
rules.rule: Enter close to the level and do not chase price beyond the defined entry band.

rules.title: Don't roll/repair broken spreads
rules.rule: Hold credit spreads to the profit or loss target and close broken ones rather than rolling or repairing them.

rules.title: Don't trade off moving averages
rules.rule: Do not use lagging indicators like moving averages as the reason for a trade.

rules.title: Every edge has capacity limits
rules.rule: Evaluate an edge by how much capital it can absorb before slippage destroys it.

rules.title: Favor relative strength leadership
rules.rule: Favor assets with price leadership versus the market, and treat relative weakness as a warning.

rules.title: Fit trading to your lifestyle
rules.rule: Pick strategies that fit your available time and trade around your life, not the reverse.

rules.title: Focus on one concept
rules.rule: Master one simple concept at a time instead of mixing many methods.

rules.title: GEX is an estimate
rules.rule: Treat GEX levels as model-based proxies of dealer positioning, not observed facts or guarantees.

rules.title: Geopolitical risk premium decays
rules.rule: Fade geopolitical risk premium once headlines calm or the ceiling is known, and revert to the fundamentals-based position.

rules.title: High IV: use spreads to cut cost
rules.rule: When implied volatility is high, use debit spreads or sell put spreads instead of buying outright options.

rules.title: Honor stops, never widen them
rules.rule: Never move a stop further away, and always take the stop-out when wrong.

rules.title: Index returns accrue overnight
rules.rule: Most index returns accrue overnight, so holding index longs from close to open captures the anomaly, especially after down days.

rules.title: Journal and review regularly
rules.rule: Keep a structured trading journal and review it regularly to improve.

rules.title: Keep an emergency fund
rules.rule: Hold 3-6 months of expenses in cash before investing the rest.

rules.title: Keep spread and condor wings narrow
rules.rule: Keep credit spread and condor wings narrow to limit tail losses.

rules.title: Lower risk on personal than prop accounts
rules.rule: Take far less risk on personal accounts than in competitions or prop evaluations.

rules.title: Macro, sentiment and price confluence
rules.rule: Enter only when macro/calendar, sentiment positioning and price action all point the same way.

rules.title: Never counter-trade at all-time highs
rules.rule: Never counter-trade at new all-time highs; fade only where old prices are accepted.

rules.title: PbD push-range-breakout pattern
rules.rule: After a strong push and a range, enter on the exit from the range with a clear stop and target.

rules.title: RSI plus Bollinger overbought pullback
rules.rule: Expect a pullback only when overbought RSI combines with an upper Bollinger Band breach or rejection.

rules.title: Reduce size during losing streaks
rules.rule: Step down risk per trade, or the number of attempts, after repeated losses.

rules.title: Risk discipline framework essential
rules.rule: Build and consistently execute a risk framework that survives normal statistical variance.

rules.title: Robustness testing dominates the work
rules.rule: Spend most of your effort on developing and robustness-testing strategies rather than coding them or watching charts.

rules.title: Roll short options for credit
rules.rule: Manage losing short puts or credit spreads by rolling, only for a net credit, or by buying back early for a small loss.

rules.title: S/R zones with role reversal
rules.rule: Treat support/resistance as zones where broken support becomes resistance.

rules.title: Sell the news on expected Fed cuts
rules.rule: Expect a possible sell-the-news reaction after a widely anticipated Fed cut, separating the decision from Powell's framing.

rules.title: Sentiment extreme plus catalyst reversal
rules.rule: Look for explosive reversals when one-sided sentiment meets an opposing catalyst.

rules.title: Thesis needs technical confirmation
rules.rule: Require price confirmation, such as a resistance break or higher highs, before acting on a fundamental or macro thesis.

rules.title: Think in probabilities, accept losses
rules.rule: Trade probabilities and accept individual losses as the cost of a consistent statistical edge.

rules.title: Time stop on stalled thesis
rules.rule: Exit or roll if the setup or thesis has not triggered or played out within the planned time window.

rules.title: Vega/extrinsic rises with time and IV
rules.rule: Expect vega and extrinsic value to be largest ATM, longer-dated and at higher IV.

rules.title: Work limit orders near the mid
rules.rule: Work option limit orders near the bid-ask midpoint instead of paying the ask.

rules.title: Trade data surprise vs consensus
rules.rule: Trade the size of a data surprise versus consensus, conditioned on quantified thresholds, not the absolute value.

rules.title: Covered call strike by expected view
rules.rule: Choose the covered-call strike by your view: OTM if you expect upside, ITM for downside protection when the stock is rich.

rules.title: High market valuation means low returns
rules.rule: Treat elevated aggregate valuations (Rule of 20, ~21x P/E, Buffett Indicator) as expensive, with low forward returns.

rules.title: Investment clock regime
rules.rule: Classify regime by growth and inflation direction, pick assets accordingly, and act only when the clock and charts agree.

rules.title: Neutral between moving averages
rules.rule: Be bullish above both key moving averages and bearish below both, and stay neutral or scale out when price is between them.

rules.title: Only trade planned edge setups
rules.rule: Take only planned trades where your edge is present and every checklist item is clear; skip impulse trades.

rules.title: Rate changes and differentials drive FX
rules.rule: Drive FX views from rate differentials and rate changes rather than absolute levels; cuts weigh on the currency.

rules.title: Stress-test liquidity and correlation breaks
rules.rule: Stress-test for liquidity evaporation, basis blowouts and correlation breaks beyond what VaR assumes.

rules.title: Be patient with solid positions
rules.rule: Give positions in solid businesses time; do not expect immediate moves.

rules.title: Buy longer-dated contracts to cut decay
rules.rule: Buy option contracts several months out rather than weeklies to reduce time decay.

rules.title: Buy quality below historical P/E
rules.rule: Buy quality stocks when their P/E is well below their historical average after a dip.

rules.title: Buy stock instead of selling CSPs
rules.rule: If you want to own a stock, especially in a crushed market, buy it at your price rather than selling cash-secured puts.

rules.title: Cap credit spread position size
rules.rule: Keep credit spreads to about 5% of the portfolio, since one loss can wipe out several winners.

rules.title: Filter divergences by oscillator extremes
rules.rule: Only count oscillator divergences that occur at extreme readings, such as RSI above 70 or a high percentile.

rules.title: LEAPs only on strong companies
rules.rule: Use LEAP calls only on fundamentally strong companies with a clear upside reason that can recover from downturns.

rules.title: Net premium flow at gamma levels
rules.rule: Confirm entries at put support, call resistance or the gamma flip with net premium flow turning your way.

rules.title: Normalize features by volatility/scale
rules.rule: Normalize thresholds and features by ATR or percentages to remove scale and volatility bias.

rules.title: Post-earnings announcement drift
rules.rule: After a big earnings-surprise gap, buy (or buy the gap test) and hold to capture post-earnings drift.

rules.title: Prefer swing horizon
rules.rule: Favor multi-day swing holds where macro works and algos don't dominate, over intraday trading.

rules.title: Recession/bear-bottom multiples
rules.rule: Size downside using recession earnings drops and multiple compression toward ~12-13x at bear-market bottoms.

rules.title: Reversals need multiple confirmations
rules.rule: Trade reversals only with aligned signals such as momentum divergence, a structure break and a resistance zone, not on overbought readings alone.

rules.title: Size pair legs by beta
rules.rule: Size pair-trade legs by relative beta, keeping the higher-beta leg smaller.

rules.title: Skip breakouts lacking stop or R:R
rules.rule: Skip direct breakouts without a sensible stop or attractive reward/risk, and wait patiently.

rules.title: Wait for actual event outcomes
rules.rule: Ahead of uncertain events, avoid pre-set scenarios and wait for the actual numbers before deriving setups.

rules.title: Yield curve recession signal
rules.rule: Treat a flat yield curve and especially its un-inversion as recession signals.

rules.title: 1-5 day holds in competitions
rules.rule: In competitions, use 1-5 day swing holds rather than intraday trading to limit fees.

rules.title: 10-wide spreads for simple math
rules.rule: Use 10-wide call spreads to make the cost-versus-max-value asymmetry easy to evaluate.

rules.title: ATR plus VIX volatility filter
rules.rule: Use ATR with VIX to judge elevated volatility and adjust entry locations.

rules.title: Account for news slippage
rules.rule: Avoid trading the news spike; trade the directional information just after it, accounting for slippage.

rules.title: Always have a bias
rules.rule: Show up with a market bias that price can change.

rules.title: Automate mechanical strategies
rules.rule: Automate mechanical strategies so human deviations don't invalidate them.

rules.title: Avoid buying weeklies on Monday
rules.rule: Avoid buying weekly options on Monday, when uncertainty and premiums are highest.

rules.title: Avoid directional bets at zero gamma
rules.rule: Avoid holding directional bets at zero gamma, which acts as a magnet.

rules.title: Avoid round-number stops
rules.rule: Avoid placing stops at round numbers where many traders cluster them.

rules.title: Avoid self-created stress
rules.rule: Trade properly to avoid creating stressful situations for yourself.

rules.title: Avoid strategy hopping
rules.rule: Stick with a plan that has an edge through losing periods while using stops.

rules.title: Be flat overnight in competitions
rules.rule: In competition trading, hold from intraday to one day and stay flat overnight where possible.

rules.title: Beware decay in volatility products
rules.rule: Beware time decay when trading volatility products.

rules.title: Bonds as information source
rules.rule: Use the bond market as an indicator rather than a trading vehicle if you cannot trade it well.

rules.title: Bullish bonds at yield extremes
rules.rule: Turn bullish on long bonds when yields hit extremes.

rules.title: Buy AI infrastructure suppliers
rules.rule: Look past headline AI winners to power, cooling and network suppliers.

rules.title: Buy ETFs in macro selloffs
rules.rule: In indiscriminate macro selloffs, buy broad-market ETFs.

rules.title: Buy ITM call spread on crushed stock
rules.rule: When a stock is crushed and IV rises, buy an ITM call spread or sell an OTM put spread at support.

rules.title: Buy back tested condor side
rules.rule: If one side of a condor is challenged, buy back the tested short strike and let the untested side expire.

rules.title: Buy mega-cap lawsuit fear
rules.rule: Treat lawsuit-driven fear in mega-caps as a buying opportunity.

rules.title: Buy options after vol cools
rules.rule: Buy options when volatility has cooled, not when premium is inflated.

rules.title: Buy straddle before big events
rules.rule: Before a pending big-move event, buy a short-dated straddle or strangle so only the move size matters.

rules.title: Buyback window bullish lean
rules.rule: Lean more bullish during buyback windows as one input, not a standalone signal.

rules.title: Cheap options aren't safer
rules.rule: Do not assume a cheaper option is safer than owning shares.

rules.title: Check strategy validity first
rules.rule: When results disappoint, examine the strategy's validity before blaming psychology.

rules.title: Choose exposures before structure
rules.rule: Define direction, timeframe, conviction and vol level first, then pick the options structure.

rules.title: Close near-the-money shorts before expiry
rules.rule: Close or manage near-the-money short strikes into expiration to avoid pin and assignment risk.

rules.title: Collar hedge for stock portfolio
rules.rule: Hedge a stock portfolio with an OTM SPY put financed by selling a further OTM call.

rules.title: Combine FA, TA and risk management
rules.rule: Combine fundamental analysis, technical analysis and risk management in one process.

rules.title: Combine price, volume and structure
rules.rule: Combine price, volume and market structure to see where big money flows.

rules.title: Compare to passive benchmark
rules.rule: Compare strategy results against a relevant passive benchmark.

rules.title: Concentration not a sell signal
rules.rule: Do not sell on concentration when leaders' earnings justify it.

rules.title: Convert QQQ gamma to NQ
rules.rule: Convert QQQ gamma strikes to NQ using the live NQ/QQQ ratio.

rules.title: Crash: stop covered calls, add convexity
rules.rule: When markets crash and vol spikes, stop selling calls and add long-vega convexity.

rules.title: Credit spreads in ranges
rules.rule: Use credit spreads in range-bound markets.

rules.title: Credit/width PoP for spreads
rules.rule: Estimate credit spread PoP from credit-to-width, and favor 80%+ far-OTM spreads.

rules.title: Cross-correlation lead-lag
rules.rule: Use cross-correlation of log returns to detect lead-lag relationships between assets.

rules.title: DCA needs quality assets
rules.rule: Choose quality businesses because DCA does not protect against declining ones.

rules.title: Daily plus hourly swing charts
rules.rule: Use 1-3 years of daily candles for context and a 10-day hourly chart for entries.

rules.title: Death cross is lagging
rules.rule: Treat a death cross as lagging, so a bottom may already be near.

rules.title: Develop with one contract first
rules.rule: Build the first strategy version with one contract and add sizing logic later.

rules.title: Diagonals for earnings events
rules.rule: For earnings or event trades, consider a diagonal that combines term-structure, long-vega and directional bets.

rules.title: Discount limit when chasing missed move
rules.rule: When chasing a missed move, set a discounted limit entry and accept the lower fill probability.

rules.title: Divergence timing sensitivity
rules.rule: Distinguish timing-robust from timing-sensitive divergences, since laggy confirmation kills the sensitive ones.

rules.title: Dollar-cost average on schedule
rules.rule: Dollar-cost average in equal chunks on a fixed schedule.

rules.title: Don't add contracts with freed buying power
rules.rule: Do not add contracts when narrower condor wings free up buying power.

rules.title: Don't buy-and-hold options
rules.rule: Do not hold options like stock since they decay toward worthless.

rules.title: Don't fight the Fed
rules.rule: Read jobless claims and CPI to anticipate Fed rate direction and trade with it.

rules.title: Don't roll deep ITM replacement calls
rules.rule: Do not roll deep ITM stock-replacement calls after rallies; let changing leverage rebalance automatically.

rules.title: ES Tuesday-to-Wednesday day-of-week tendency
rules.rule: Study the ES tendency of buying the Tuesday open and exiting at the Wednesday open as a day-of-week effect.

rules.title: Enter when Fed changes direction
rules.rule: Position for a long trend when the Fed changes policy direction.

rules.title: Exit fast on contrary news
rules.rule: When a news surprise contradicts your position, exit or hedge quickly during the market's digestion window.

rules.title: Exit when moves stop being impulsive
rules.rule: Exit when price action stops being impulsive and turns choppy.

rules.title: Expect mean reversion of returns
rules.rule: After long above-average returns, expect more muted future returns.

rules.title: Fed cuts start late
rules.rule: Expect recession to have begun and cuts to be aggressive once the Fed starts cutting.

rules.title: Fed delivers highly priced hikes
rules.rule: Assume the Fed delivers when a hike is priced at ~93%+.

rules.title: Fed more reliable than BoJ
rules.rule: Treat Fed signals as more reliable to trade than BoJ signals.

rules.title: Fed pivot not guaranteed bullish
rules.rule: Do not assume a Fed pivot or lower rates guarantees a stock rally.

rules.title: Find your high-probability markets
rules.rule: Identify which markets and conditions give you higher probabilities.

rules.title: Fixed routine and review hours
rules.rule: Fix a routine with set market-review hours and consistent sleep to reduce decisions and support discipline.

rules.title: Fundamentals where, technicals how
rules.rule: Use fundamentals to know where and when to look, and technicals for direction, entry, stop and target.

rules.title: Harvest tax losses
rules.rule: Sell losing positions to harvest tax losses.

rules.title: High IV isn't directional
rules.rule: Read high IV as an expected big move in either direction, not upside.

rules.title: High IV premium is risky
rules.rule: Recognize that juicy premium in high IV comes with much higher risk.

rules.title: High win-probability threshold
rules.rule: Take only trades with roughly 70-80% estimated win probability.

rules.title: Hold bonds to rebalance into stocks
rules.rule: Hold bonds so you can sell them to buy stocks during a recession.

rules.title: ITM cash-secured puts capture drift
rules.rule: Consider striking cash-secured puts in the money to capture equity drift.

rules.title: ITM for choppy, OTM for trending
rules.rule: Use ITM options for slow, choppy stocks and OTM options for fast-trending movers.

rules.title: IV is a dial, not switch
rules.rule: Adjust strikes and size to the IV environment rather than trading only in high IV.

rules.title: Implied vs expected realized movement
rules.rule: Sell defined-risk premium when you expect less movement than priced, and buy options when you expect more.

rules.title: Inflation compresses P/E
rules.rule: Expect lower P/E multiples when inflation is higher.

rules.title: Inflation reassessment threshold
rules.rule: Reassess the inflation leg if CPI/core PCE or Truflation stays above ~3%.

rules.title: Inside-day buy-stop setup
rules.rule: At an important level, place a buy-stop above the inside-day candle with the stop below the 200-day MA.

rules.title: Jobless claims warning
rules.rule: Treat claims above a threshold for several weeks as a first labor-market warning.

rules.title: KOSPI reversal lead
rules.rule: Use KOSPI reversals after consecutive down sessions as a lead for a US-open bounce.

rules.title: LEAP target at pre-crash high
rules.rule: Use the prior pre-crash high region as the profit target for recovery LEAP trades.

rules.title: Late speculative runs are fragile
rules.rule: Expect late speculative rallies to top on small doubts.

rules.title: Learn with small real money
rules.rule: Learn new markets with small real money rather than demo accounts.

rules.title: Leveraged ETF decay
rules.rule: Account for volatility decay in leveraged ETFs.

rules.title: Long deferred after front-month collapse
rules.rule: When a front-month commodity collapses, go long deferred contracts or producers instead.

rules.title: Long strangle flat risk
rules.rule: Remember a long strangle loses on both legs if the stock stays flat.

rules.title: Long strangle leg management
rules.rule: On a long strangle, cash the winning leg gradually and exit the losing leg once the move resolves.

rules.title: Look for catalysts
rules.rule: For growth trades, seek catalysts such as earnings, launches or industry shifts.

rules.title: Low VIX hurts systematic edges
rules.rule: Expect systematic edges to suffer when VIX is compressed below ~15.

rules.title: Macro as directional filter
rules.rule: Use macro as a long-term directional filter and trade in the conviction direction.

rules.title: Macro conviction over 2-4 day horizon
rules.rule: Apply macro conviction over a roughly 2-4 day horizon to set intraday direction.

rules.title: Match R:R to trading style
rules.rule: Keep targets consistent with stop size and style; don't take day-trade profits on swing-trade risk.

rules.title: Match long-delta structure to conviction
rules.rule: Use deep ITM calls for low conviction and low-delta OTM calls for extreme conviction.

rules.title: Mine academic papers for ideas
rules.rule: Use academic papers as a hypothesis source, extracting value rather than copying.

rules.title: Minimum credit and exit on doubling
rules.rule: Set a minimum credit when selling spreads and reduce or exit if the spread doubles.

rules.title: Modular macro analysis
rules.rule: Use a modular analysis process, applying only the relevant blocks.

rules.title: Need full option-buying pattern
rules.rule: Act only on a complete pattern of option buying, not on a single large print.

rules.title: Net drift premium flow
rules.rule: Use net premium flow drift as a read on bullish or bearish dealer hedging flow.

rules.title: Net drift unreliable around FOMC
rules.rule: Discount net drift signals around FOMC, because the market is pricing the event.

rules.title: Never stretch risk limits
rules.rule: Never stretch risk limits temporarily after a good P&L run.

rules.title: No fixed profit targets
rules.rule: Avoid fixed daily or monthly profit targets that force bad trades.

rules.title: Non-linear theta decay
rules.rule: Remember that theta decay is non-linear and erodes static ATM long options to zero.

rules.title: One options position at a time
rules.rule: Beginners should open one well-researched options position at a time.

rules.title: Overnight range breakout
rules.rule: Go long Nasdaq futures on a close above the 4-5 p.m. ET range in the first hour after reopen, with a 1:1 target, and exit by the European open.

rules.title: Own real assets in inflation
rules.rule: In persistent inflation, own stocks and hard assets over cash.

rules.title: PoP via breakeven delta
rules.rule: Approximate vertical spread probability of profit using the delta at the breakeven strike.

rules.title: Pre-earnings run-ups shrink moves
rules.rule: Expect smaller post-earnings moves after big pre-earnings run-ups.

rules.title: Prefer zones overlapping others' zones
rules.rule: Prefer zones that overlap other traders' approaches.

rules.title: Price options probabilistically
rules.rule: Value options from probability-weighted payoffs, not the most likely price.

rules.title: Protect profits at exit
rules.rule: Judge trades by the exit and protect profits so winners don't become losers.

rules.title: Put credit spreads 1-3 weeks out
rules.rule: Choose put credit spread expirations about 1-3 weeks out for faster theta decay and adaptability.

rules.title: RSI 70/30 overbought/oversold
rules.rule: Use RSI above 70 as overbought and below 30 as oversold.

rules.title: RSI support bounce confirms uptrend
rules.rule: Confirm an intact uptrend by daily RSI bouncing around 55 and Bollinger Band shifts.

rules.title: Rebalance delta-neutral hedges
rules.rule: Rebalance delta-neutral hedges as delta changes.

rules.title: Recession investing is defensive
rules.rule: In recessions aim to preserve capital, not get rich.

rules.title: Rent the winning hedge
rules.rule: If your hedge keeps beating your risk asset, allocate to the hedge rather than chase beta.

rules.title: Require multi-month data trends
rules.rule: Require several months of trend in data before drawing macro conclusions.

rules.title: Research must reject strategies
rules.rule: Ensure your research process can reject losing strategies.

rules.title: Risk first, overlays last
rules.rule: Prioritize risk first, investing second and option overlays third.

rules.title: Risk reversal in targetless momentum
rules.rule: In strong momentum with no clear target, sell an OTM put at a level you'd own and buy an OTM call.

rules.title: Risk-on vs safe-haven currencies
rules.rule: Buy growth currencies in optimism and JPY/CHF/USD as safe havens.

rules.title: Roll calls at 60-70 delta
rules.rule: Buy ~40-delta calls and sell or roll them when they reach 60-70 delta.

rules.title: Rolling doesn't erase losses
rules.rule: Recognize that rolling a tested short option does not erase the loss already incurred.

rules.title: S&P favors mean reversion
rules.rule: Use mean-reversion rather than breakout logic on the S&P 500.

rules.title: S&P/gold ratio risk warning
rules.rule: Treat a monthly S&P/gold close below a key level with negative slope as elevated equity risk.

rules.title: SMA trend scorecard
rules.rule: Score trend -3 to +3 from the 20/50 SMAs and their slopes, and set exposure accordingly.

rules.title: Sample at information-bearing events
rules.rule: Sample observations at information-bearing events rather than forecasting every candle.

rules.title: Seek edges in under-covered stocks
rules.rule: Look for edges in small/mid caps with low institutional coverage.

rules.title: Short-dated directional needs timing
rules.rule: Recognize that short-dated directional options need correct direction, magnitude and timing to profit.

rules.title: Size options from underlying stop
rules.rule: Size options by the projected delta-based loss at the underlying stop.

rules.title: Size so stops are emotionally neutral
rules.rule: Size so that no single day's stop or profit changes your life emotionally.

rules.title: Size stock replacement by option leverage
rules.rule: Size deep ITM calls by option leverage, not like shares.

rules.title: Skip earnings priced at ~2 SD
rules.rule: Skip an earnings trade if options already price in about two standard deviations of movement.

rules.title: Sold puts carry crash risk
rules.rule: Remember sector crashes can drag quality names down 50%+, exposing sold puts.

rules.title: Stand down on volatile earnings condor
rules.rule: Skip an earnings condor if volatile activity shows into the close.

rules.title: Straddle prices earnings move
rules.rule: Estimate the priced-in earnings move from the ATM straddle price.

rules.title: Strike distance scales with time
rules.rule: Go further OTM only with more time to expiration; keep strikes near the money when time is short.

rules.title: Systems decay from amplitude change
rules.rule: Monitor move amplitude and intraday persistence as the cause of system breakdown.

rules.title: TA guides through macro noise
rules.rule: Use technical analysis as the objective guide through macro noise.

rules.title: Tech vs S&P P/E convergence
rules.rule: Treat tech leaders as discounted when their forward P/E converges with the S&P 500's.

rules.title: Time options from underlying structure
rules.rule: Time directional option entries from the underlying's price structure, using option flow only as confirmation.

rules.title: Trade from concepts, not fixed plan
rules.rule: Trade from concepts rather than a rigid step-by-step plan, since every session differs.

rules.title: Trail stop to breakeven early
rules.rule: Protect the downside by trailing the stop to entry or taking partial profits early.

rules.title: Two types of bear bottoms
rules.rule: Distinguish stimulus-rescued crash bottoms from slow exhaustion bottoms when the Fed is constrained.

rules.title: Underweight politically risky markets
rules.rule: Underweight markets with high political or intervention uncertainty.

rules.title: Use negative balance protection
rules.rule: Use brokers with negative balance protection for leveraged CFDs.

rules.title: Use real executed-trade data
rules.rule: Verify your data is real exchange execution data before trusting models.

rules.title: VIX above Bollinger study
rules.rule: Study asset returns after VIX/VixFix closes above its upper Bollinger Band.

rules.title: VIX trendline break marks bottom
rules.rule: Treat a VIX ascending trendline breakdown as a short-term equity bottom.

rules.title: Vertical or BWB with clear target
rules.rule: In a trending market with a clear target, use a vertical call spread or broken-wing butterfly capped at the target.

rules.title: Volatility is opportunity
rules.rule: Treat volatility as opportunity rather than threat.

rules.title: Weak Treasury auctions hurt growth
rules.rule: Treat weak Treasury auctions as a yield-lifting headwind for growth stocks.

rules.title: Weekend watchlist preparation
rules.rule: Use weekends to scan markets and build the next week's watchlist.

rules.title: 10/20-day MA bear cross on QQQ and sector ETFs
rules.rule: Watch for the 10-day moving average crossing below the 20-day on QQQ and leading sector ETFs as confirmation that momentum is deteriorating.

rules.title: Avoid overnight swings when VIX and gaps are large
rules.rule: Avoid overnight swing trades when the VIX is elevated and gaps are large.

rules.title: Be biggest at the start and add fast when right
rules.rule: Be bigger at the start of a good trade and add quickly when you are right.

rules.title: Short failed rallies into the 50-day MA
rules.rule: Short a daily rally into the 50-day moving average that fails to reclaim it after a breakdown.

rules.title: Covered call strike at or above price target
rules.rule: Place covered calls at a strike no lower than your price target.

rules.title: When in doubt, get out
rules.rule: When in doubt, get out of the position and reassess; you can always get back in.

rules.title: Push size only with defined max loss
rules.rule: Push size only when you have a clear stop or a defined max loss such as an option structure.

rules.title: Breakouts need volume and RVOL confirmation
rules.rule: Only take breakout trades when volume confirms the break and relative volume is elevated; exit if volume does not confirm.

rules.title: Exit move-to-move trades on 21 EMA close
rules.rule: Exit a move-to-move trade when price closes below a trailing 21 EMA for a long (above for a short), or when an accelerated trendline breaks.

rules.title: Exit trend trades at first counter swing
rules.rule: Exit a trend trade at the first higher low in a downtrend or first lower high in an uptrend.

rules.title: Buy tight pullbacks to short-term SMAs in strong stocks
rules.rule: For trend swings, buy a strong stock after it pulls back and tightens near the 5, 10 and 20-day SMAs, entering when it reclaims the 10-day SMA and trailing the stop under the prior day's low.

rules.title: Keep risk small while new
rules.rule: Keep risk small while you are new, because you are at your least skilled now.

rules.title: Manage a trade on its entry timeframe
rules.rule: Enter, exit, and manage a trade on the same time frame.

rules.title: Trade new strategies tiny for the first 20 reps
rules.rule: Trade a new strategy live very small for the first 20 tagged reps before scaling up.

rules.title: Roll LEAPS up at 0.9+ delta
rules.rule: Roll a LEAP up in strike when its delta reaches about 0.9-0.95, since its leverage has shrunk.

rules.title: Buy ITM options for a low break-even
rules.rule: Buy in-the-money options for a low break-even rather than out-of-the-money options; choose by break-even, not by what you can afford.

rules.title: Sell options back; do not exercise early
rules.rule: Close options by selling them back to the market rather than exercising them early, to keep the extrinsic value.

rules.title: Understand assignment before selling options
rules.rule: Learn how assignment and the strategy's profit-and-loss math work before trading spreads or selling options.

rules.title: Sell premium 30-45 DTE near 0.3 delta
rules.rule: Sell cash-secured puts and covered calls about 30-45 days to expiration, starting near 0.3 delta.

rules.title: Covered calls above cost basis after assignment
rules.rule: After put assignment, sell covered calls above your adjusted cost basis.

rules.title: Roll only when credit/collateral return justifies it
rules.rule: Keep rolling a short put only while credit divided by collateral gives an acceptable return for the time locked up.

rules.title: PMCC: ~0.7-delta long, ~0.3-delta short 30-45 DTE
rules.rule: For a poor man's covered call, buy the long call in the money near 0.7 delta at least three months out and sell the short call near 0.3 delta 30-45 days out.

rules.title: Long-dated debit call spread: ~0.6-delta long leg
rules.rule: For a long-dated debit call spread, buy the long leg near 0.6 delta about a year out on a liquid underlying and sell the short leg at or out of the money.

rules.title: Scale spreads by width, not count
rules.rule: Scale a spread's risk and reward by widening the strikes rather than opening many spreads.

rules.title: Small accounts: avoid high-probability credit spreads
rules.rule: With a small account, avoid high-probability credit spreads whose max loss dwarfs the credit.

rules.title: Do not hold options through a stock split
rules.rule: Avoid holding options through a stock split, because the adjusted contracts become illiquid.

rules.title: LEAPS over futures for long-term leverage
rules.rule: Use LEAPS rather than futures for long-term leveraged holds, because of convergence and contango.

rules.title: Use far-dated call spreads when a LEAP breaks the cap
rules.rule: If a LEAP would exceed 10% of the portfolio, use a far-dated debit call spread instead.

rules.title: Don't invest money needed within a year
rules.rule: Do not invest money you will need within about a year.

rules.title: Minimum account size before options
rules.rule: Wait until the account reaches about $1,000-$1,500 before trading options; grow a small account with shares first.

rules.title: Be able to survive a 50% market drop
rules.rule: Keep your exposure such that you could handle a 50% drop in the stock market.

rules.title: Don't buy just under tested resistance
rules.rule: Do not buy right below a resistance level that price has already hit twice.

rules.title: Buy channel bottom, sell top or middle
rules.rule: In a price channel, buy near the bottom and sell near the top or middle.

rules.title: Time in the market beats timing it
rules.rule: Time in the market beats timing the market.

rules.title: Buy companies you know and use
rules.rule: Invest in companies whose products you use or would use, that are profitable or close to it, and that are not obscure penny stocks.

rules.title: Buy the story only when fundamentals back it
rules.rule: Use a company's story as a reason to buy only when the fundamentals support it.

rules.title: Check cash runway against the thesis horizon
rules.rule: Check the company's cash runway: it must survive long enough for the thesis to play out.

rules.title: Market cap near cash can be a buy
rules.rule: A stock whose market cap roughly equals its cash on hand is pricing in no future and can be a buy.

rules.title: Wait quarters after a fraud short report
rules.rule: When a short report alleges inflated earnings, wait a few quarters for confirmation before buying.

rules.title: Read the FOMC projections, not just the decision
rules.rule: Watch the FOMC economic projections and the projected rate path, not just the rate decision.

rules.title: Don't buy at the IPO; wait
rules.rule: Do not rush to buy at an IPO; wait and see how it trades.

rules.title: Prefer reinvestors over dividend payers
rules.rule: Prefer companies that reinvest earnings in growth over dividend payers.

rules.title: Hold a year+ for long-term capital gains
rules.rule: Hold winners a year or more to get the long-term capital gains tax rate.

rules.title: Keep a standing cash reserve as dry powder
rules.rule: Keep a standing cash sleeve (at least about 10%) as dry powder so you can buy when quality assets go on sale instead of being forced to sell.

rules.title: Small in pullbacks, size up when momentum returns
rules.rule: Keep positions small and protect capital during pullbacks; deploy heavily only when momentum returns and the market breaks higher.

rules.title: Weight by how real the cash flows are
rules.rule: Put the biggest weights where cash flows already exist and the smallest where there is only a story.

rules.title: Hedge longs with a short instead of selling
rules.rule: Hedge long holdings with a short on a correlated index or risk asset, or offsetting positions, instead of selling the core.

rules.title: Core, swing and tactical sleeves
rules.rule: Split the book into core, swing and tactical sleeves; only the small tactical sleeve reacts to headline weeks.

rules.title: Position on peer and customer read-throughs
rules.rule: Use peer and customer earnings, capex and leader commentary as a read-through to position before a related company reports.

rules.title: Avoid hyped IPOs at extreme sales multiples
rules.rule: Avoid hyped IPOs at extreme revenue multiples backed by underwriter research; retail is the exit liquidity.

rules.title: Mega-IPO clusters are a top signal
rules.rule: Treat clusters of mega IPOs as a top signal and expect other stocks to bleed as money is freed for them.

rules.title: Play hyped listings through proxies
rules.rule: Play a hyped listing through listed peers, proxies or large shareholders instead of paying the listing-day premium.

rules.title: Read core CPI, not the headline
rules.rule: On CPI day, react to core inflation rather than the oil-driven headline number.

rules.title: When good news gets sold, sellers control
rules.rule: When strong earnings fail to hold a bid into the close, assume sellers are in control and protect capital.

rules.title: Buy ahead of index inclusion flows
rules.rule: Buy names on a path to major index inclusion or a US listing before the forced passive buying arrives.

rules.title: Let mechanical flows clear before buying
rules.rule: When a dip or discount comes from index or rebalancing flows rather than the business, let the flows clear and then buy.

rules.title: Follow government stakes and funding
rules.rule: Favor companies and sectors with direct government equity stakes, backing or multi-year funding commitments.

rules.title: Industry-leader adoption as a signal
rules.rule: Treat an industry leader adopting, investing in or partnering with a company as a strong signal.

rules.title: Pick the industry tailwind before the company
rules.rule: Start with an industry that has a tailwind; underwrite the pie growing rather than one company winning outright.

rules.title: Moat test: switching costs, pricing power, data
rules.rule: Favor companies with a real moat: customers would suffer without them, high switching costs, or proprietary data.

rules.title: Accelerating revenue, raised guidance, expanding margins
rules.rule: Favor businesses with accelerating revenue, raised guidance, booked demand and revenue growing faster than costs.

rules.title: Cyclicals with multi-year contracted minimums
rules.rule: In cyclical sectors, favor companies with multi-year contracts, committed volumes and guaranteed minimums.

rules.title: Smallest name or proxy for most torque
rules.rule: Within a theme, prefer the smallest company or lower-cap proxies with leverage to the underlying for the most upside.

rules.title: Toll-booth businesses that win either way
rules.rule: Favor businesses that take a fee on every transaction or win no matter which competitor wins.

rules.title: Judge pre-revenue names on pipeline
rules.rule: For pre-revenue qualification-cycle companies, judge on pipeline growth rather than trailing revenue.

rules.title: Index level from forward EPS x normal multiple
rules.rule: Value the index as forward earnings times a normal multiple (about 20x) to judge its fair level.

rules.title: Cyclicals look cheapest at the top
rules.rule: Do not buy cyclicals because they look cheap at peak earnings; they usually top months before earnings peak.

rules.title: Judge what the price already expects
rules.rule: Separate the business from the stock: judge valuation by the expectations already baked into the price.

rules.title: Rotate into cheap laggards; wait for capital to return
rules.rule: Rotate toward quality names and sectors that never ran and stayed cheap, and buy a sector's dip once capital rotates back in.

rules.title: Yen and JGB yields as early warning
rules.rule: Watch the yen and Japanese government bond yields as an early warning for carry unwinds and higher US yields.

rules.title: Oil leads geopolitical outcomes
rules.rule: Use the oil price, not headlines, as the leading indicator of geopolitical deal outcomes.

rules.title: A ceasefire is not a resolution
rules.rule: Do not treat a geopolitical pause or ceasefire as a resolution; expect oil spikes to return.

rules.title: Markets test a new Fed chair
rules.rule: Expect a pullback of about 10% around a Fed chair transition and do not rush to buy ahead of it.

rules.title: Draw ranges at the wicks
rules.rule: Draw range highs and lows at the wicks, not the candle bodies.

rules.title: Repeated wicks at highs signal exhaustion
rules.rule: Treat repeated wicks at the highs and rounding tops as exhaustion of the move.

rules.title: Never bet more than Kelly
rules.rule: Size bets at or below the Kelly fraction (for even-money bets, the edge), and below full Kelly because the true edge is uncertain; overbetting destroys growth.

rules.title: Volatility forecasts lag sudden crashes
rules.rule: Do not rely on backward-looking volatility forecasts to cut size before a crash that follows a calm stretch; they react only afterward.

rules.title: Drops raise volatility more than rallies
rules.rule: Expect volatility to rise more after a drop than after an equal rally, and treat symmetric volatility models as underestimating risk right after a sell-off.

rules.title: Risk parity: equal risk contribution
rules.rule: Weight asset classes so each contributes the same share of portfolio risk (simplest form: inverse-volatility weights) instead of letting stocks dominate a 60/40 mix.

rules.title: Anchor allocation on market weights, tilt by view confidence
rules.rule: Start from market-cap weights and tilt toward your own return views only in proportion to your confidence, since small return-estimate errors push optimizer weights to extremes.

rules.title: Prove mean reversion before trading it
rules.rule: Trade mean reversion only in series with a statistically proven pull back (spreads, ratios, rates), using a strict t-statistic limit of about -3 and the half-life.

rules.title: Momentum crashes on sharp rebounds
rules.rule: Expect momentum portfolios to suffer sudden large losses when markets turn sharply and past losers rebound.

rules.title: Favor low-volatility stocks over lottery stocks
rules.rule: Favor calm, low-volatility stocks over wild lottery-like stocks, which have historically earned less.

rules.title: Pair VaR with expected shortfall
rules.rule: Assume fat tails and add expected shortfall to value at risk, since VaR says nothing about how bad the worst days get.

rules.title: Chart patterns lack proven predictive power
rules.rule: Do not trade chart patterns on the belief that they predict; pattern rules have not survived honest tests for data snooping and costs.

rules.title: Delta-hedge short options and rebalance
rules.rule: Hedge short options with delta shares and rebalance repeatedly as delta changes.

rules.title: Check option quotes with put-call parity
rules.rule: Use put-call parity (call minus put equals stock minus present value of strike) to check option quotes.

rules.title: Stop-out surprise test
rules.rule: Before entering, ask how surprised you would be to get stopped out, and skip the trade unless the answer is very surprised.

rules.title: Alerts propose, the trader decides
rules.rule: Build a standalone scanner that alerts only when every setup criterion is met, with entry, stop and target, then make the take-or-skip decision yourself.

rules.title: One index per idea
rules.rule: Do not hold the same direction on NQ and ES at once, because it doubles the risk on one idea.

rules.title: Take a week off after a blow-up
rules.rule: After blowing an account, take a week off before trading again.

rules.title: No trading after a bad night's sleep
rules.rule: Do not trade the day after a bad night of sleep.

rules.title: Use discretion only to skip trades
rules.rule: Keep a human take-or-skip step over a mechanical system, using discretion only to skip valid signals and never to take trades that break the rules.

rules.title: Trade only from a focused desk
rules.rule: Trade only from a desk or quiet place where you can focus, not on the move.

rules.title: Hide P&L while trading
rules.rule: Hide the P&L display while trading if you catch yourself chasing dollars.

rules.title: Weight recent strategy performance
rules.rule: Reject a strategy that has lost over the recent period even if its long-run average is positive, and favor the strategies that were strongest in recent weeks.

rules.title: Check rolling win-rate stability
rules.rule: Check that the rolling win rate stays in a stable range above break-even and that cumulative R grows steadily.

rules.title: Validate and model each market separately
rules.rule: Test every rule and build every model separately for each market and timeframe, because a fix on one index often fails on another.

rules.title: Fix low trade frequency with more strategies
rules.rule: When filtering leaves a good strategy that trades rarely, raise its frequency by tweaking it or add more strategies.

rules.title: Freeze a system that meets its target
rules.rule: Stop optimizing once a strategy meets a preset performance requirement, and do not rework a system that is making money.

rules.title: One small change per optimizer step
rules.rule: Limit an AI optimizer to one small change per iteration, such as moving a stop or target or adding or removing one filter.

rules.title: Textbook strategies fail when run mechanically
rules.rule: Do not expect textbook retail strategies run mechanically to be profitable or to pass prop evaluations after costs.

rules.title: Turn trade notes into tested formulas
rules.rule: Have AI turn descriptive trade notes into measurable formulas and test each one against your past trades.

rules.title: Stop posting trades if the audience sways you
rules.rule: Stop posting your trades publicly if audience pressure affects your decisions.

rules.title: Collect a wide sample before narrowing
rules.rule: Do not narrow times, assets and criteria too early; collect a wide sample of live trades first and filter gradually on the data.

rules.title: Hindsight-test past days first
rules.rule: Mark up past days in hindsight to learn what your winning trades look like before trying to trade them live.

rules.title: Map event scenarios before the release
rules.rule: Before a scheduled data release, map outcome ranges with probabilities and expected reactions, review the last reaction, and rehearse your response to each scenario.

rules.title: Drop trades the data invalidate
rules.rule: Cancel a planned trade when new economic data remove its reason.

rules.title: Don't short after a hawkish hold
rules.rule: Do not short a currency right after its central bank delivers a hawkish hold.

rules.title: Trade AUD as a China proxy
rules.rule: Sell AUD on disappointing Chinese news and favor AUD and NZD after strong China data.

rules.title: Buy selloffs after credit normalizes
rules.rule: Wait to buy a selloff until high-yield spreads are back below their pre-selloff reading, and for speculative names until CCC spreads narrow versus BBB.

rules.title: Buy bonds only when yields actually fall
rules.rule: Buy long bonds only when long yields are actually falling and a breakout holds its retest; a flatter curve alone is no reason.

rules.title: Auction yield as rebound validity line
rules.rule: Mark the pre-auction Treasury yield and trust a stock rebound only while yields stay below it and stocks hold the recovery.

rules.title: Exit at stop, 2R or 20 sessions
rules.rule: Exit at the stop, at a gain of twice the initial risk, or after 20 trading sessions, whichever comes first.

rules.title: Scratch at breakeven on a counter signal
rules.rule: Exit at breakeven when a signal appears against the trade.

rules.title: Close when a cross ignores its legs
rules.rule: When a cross rate fails to move as its two legs imply, assume institutional flow is on the other side and close the trade.

rules.title: Size bond risk by duration
rules.rule: Estimate a bond holding's risk as its duration times a plausible rise in yields.

rules.title: Check the hedge still protects
rules.rule: Monitor whether your hedge still protects the portfolio, not the level of the hedge asset.

rules.title: Don't hedge with a shared driver
rules.rule: Do not rely on an asset to hedge another when both share the same driver, as gold and equities can.

rules.title: Buy protection while it is cheap
rules.rule: Add hedges or volatility upside while protection is still cheap, such as when VIX is unusually low before an FOMC meeting.

rules.title: Know each instrument's worst case
rules.rule: Know the worst-case outcome of every instrument you trade, including losses beyond your deposit.

rules.title: Leveraged ETFs are not confirmation
rules.rule: Do not use a leveraged ETF as independent confirmation; check its index, daily leverage and overlap with your holdings.

rules.title: Decide currency hedging on foreign assets
rules.rule: When buying foreign stocks or funds, decide on currency hedging and check whether the fund or share class actually hedges.

rules.title: Risk less when a pullback comes first
rules.rule: Use smaller risk, such as half a percent, when you expect a pullback before the entry works.

rules.title: Hold Fed trades one to three sessions
rules.rule: Hold Fed-event trades for one to three sessions and reassess at each close.

rules.title: News is traded in each time zone
rules.rule: Expect portfolio managers in each time zone to act on news in their own hours, and use the London and US sessions as further entries.

rules.title: Wait days before acting on headlines
rules.rule: Judge a political headline or event by how assets trade over the following days, waiting up to 72 hours before acting.

rules.title: Anticipate calendar institutional flows
rules.rule: Anticipate quarter-end pension rebalancing and month-end closing flows from MOC imbalances and CTA signals.

rules.title: Rising VIX at highs is a warning
rules.rule: Treat a rising VIX while stocks are still high as smart money buying protection.

rules.title: Quiet VVIX means smoke, not fire
rules.rule: Watch VVIX as an early warning; if it stays quiet while VIX is high, treat the drop as smoke, not fire.

rules.title: Financing stress ratio dashboard
rules.rule: Treat two of QUAL/IWM, SPY/XLRE and high-yield spreads at new 20-day highs as financing pressure, and all three as stress spreading into credit.

rules.title: Watch internal ratios for rotation
rules.rule: Watch sector and index ratios such as XSD/SMH, SMH/QQQ, IWM/QQQ and VXN/VIX to spot rotation before the index breaks.

rules.title: 2-year yield and small-cap leadership
rules.rule: Read a falling 2-year yield with Russell 2000 leadership as pressure easing, and the reverse as pressure building.

rules.title: 2s10s curve leads ISM by a year
rules.rule: Use the 2s10s curve advanced by one year as a leading signal for the ISM manufacturing index.

rules.title: Fast 2-year drop means recession fear
rules.rule: Treat a sharp, fast drop in the 2-year yield as the market bracing for emergency cuts and recession; a slow drift is calm.

rules.title: Diagnose why long yields rise
rules.rule: Check the term premium, inflation expectations and the dollar to see whether rising long yields reflect growth or fiscal pressure from deficits.

rules.title: Intervention needs fundamental confirmation
rules.rule: Treat FX intervention as a catalyst only; confirm a reversal with a narrowing rate spread, capital flows, reserves and the current account.

rules.title: Commodity currencies as risk clues
rules.rule: Watch AUD, NZD, CAD and AUD/CHF as early clues of risk sentiment and cues for index trades, not as buy signals.

rules.title: Oil as inflation direction proxy
rules.rule: Use oil prices as a proxy for the direction of inflation and therefore central bank action.

rules.title: Back-month oil strength means sticky inflation
rules.rule: When back-month oil rallies harder than the front, treat inflation as structural and avoid long duration.

rules.title: Track the full energy cost chain
rules.rule: Do not watch Brent alone; track the diesel-crude spread, bunker prices, freight rates and margins.

rules.title: Trust the broad market over the index
rules.rule: When bonds, currencies, commodities and volatility disagree with the equity index, trust them; when stocks and oil disagree, trust oil.

rules.title: Tops roll over in sequence
rules.rule: Spot a top as small names, then megacaps, then manufacturers, then equipment makers roll over in sequence.

rules.title: Bonds fail as hedge in inflation shocks
rules.rule: In high-inflation regimes and energy supply shocks, expect bonds to fall with stocks and favor gold and energy as hedges.

rules.title: Avoid duration in a bear steepener
rules.rule: In a bear steepener, avoid long-duration bonds, utilities, consumer staples and real estate.

rules.title: Classify oil moves as demand or supply
rules.rule: Classify an oil move as demand-driven or supply-driven before judging its effect on bonds and the portfolio.

rules.title: Oil supply shock rule of thumb
rules.rule: Estimate an oil supply shock as roughly a 4% price rise for every 1% of supply lost.

rules.title: Energy spikes favor USD over EUR
rules.rule: When oil or gas spikes, favor the dollar over the euro because Europe imports its energy.

rules.title: Energy inflation traps central banks
rules.rule: Expect a central bank to be trapped when energy lifts inflation while growth weakens; hikes do not cure energy inflation.

rules.title: The unpriced outcome is the surprise
rules.rule: When one outcome is heavily priced, treat the opposite outcome as the bigger surprise the market must unprice.

rules.title: Don't buy a liquidity crisis early
rules.rule: Do not buy into a liquidity crisis until volatility comes down; expect forced margin selling even in assets like gold.

rules.title: No Fed put while inflation runs hot
rules.rule: Do not count on a Fed put while six-month inflation runs above the 12-month rate and most components exceed 3%.

rules.title: Judge a rate cut by its reason
rules.rule: Judge a rate cut by why it was needed, not as good news by itself.

rules.title: Favor cash when bills out-yield stocks
rules.rule: Compare T-bill yields with equity dividend yields and favor cash when bills pay far more.

rules.title: Pick CSP names by IV, chart and trigger
rules.rule: Choose cash-secured put candidates with high implied volatility, a clear chart structure and a fundamental or macro trigger.

rules.title: Covered calls are not downside protection
rules.rule: Use covered calls only with a sideways to moderately bullish view and willingness to sell at the strike, not as downside protection.

rules.title: Sell condors after VIX calms
rules.rule: Sell iron condors only once VIX has calmed back down after a spike.

rules.title: Manage debit spread legs together
rules.rule: In a debit spread, accept that the debit can be lost and profit is capped, and manage both legs together.

rules.title: Trade observed flows, not expectations
rules.rule: Trade the flows you see, not your expectations.

rules.title: Follow the price of money, not Fed guesses
rules.rule: Do not try to predict the Fed; follow what markets price for rates.

rules.title: Analyze from macro down to the stock
rules.rule: Analyze top down: macro, regional markets, sector, peers, then the stock.

rules.title: Seek an information edge on flows
rules.rule: Seek an edge by knowing more or knowing earlier, especially about who is buying and selling.

rules.title: Match data dates and components
rules.rule: Match observation dates and periods, and separate components such as real yields and breakevens, before comparing data.

rules.title: Own bullion, not miners, for gold
rules.rule: Do not use gold mining stocks as a substitute for gold; confirm the fund owns bullion.

rules.title: Check cash flow behind earnings
rules.rule: Check that free cash flow after capex keeps pace with earnings and can fund dividends and buildouts without fresh debt.

rules.title: Stress-test income without specials
rules.rule: Separate earnings-linked dividends from special payments and stress-test income without the special part.

rules.title: Check refinancing costs on debt
rules.rule: Check a company's debt maturities and the cost of replacing old debt, since higher interest cuts payouts.

rules.title: Extra yield is pay for extra risk
rules.rule: Before reaching for yield, check spread, duration, fiscal and inflation risk, currency and hedging cost, and compare with safe deposits.

rules.title: Check EPS against dilution and buybacks
rules.rule: Before celebrating EPS growth, check total profit growth, diluted share count and the price paid for buybacks.

rules.title: Stress-test valuation with lower earnings
rules.rule: Cut your earnings assumption and recalculate whether you would still pay today's price.

rules.title: Judge sovereign debt by growth vs rates
rules.rule: Judge sovereign debt by nominal growth versus borrowing costs, primary balance, maturity profile and currency, not the debt ratio alone.

rules.title: Debate outcome X01
rules.rule: Scale in only when total size, add levels and one never-lowered invalidation level are fixed before the first entry. Adding because the price is lower is averaging down.

rules.title: Debate outcome X02
rules.rule: Every position has a stop at its invalidation level from entry, and size is set from that distance. For long options the premium is the maximum loss, so size the premium as if the stop will gap.

rules.title: Debate outcome X03
rules.rule: Default to defined-risk structures (debit spreads, credit spreads, long options, cash-secured puts). No undefined-risk short premium.

rules.title: Debate outcome X05
rules.rule: A stop is not a maximum-loss limit; position size is the real control. Keep per-name concentration inside the owner caps.

rules.title: Debate outcome X06
rules.rule: Do not pre-position for a post-event move (FOMC, CPI, earnings). Going flat is not the default either: size every open position so an event gap through the stop is affordable.

rules.title: Debate outcome X07
rules.rule: Do not use margin to buy dips. Options premium is paid in cash and capped per name.

rules.title: Debate outcome X09
rules.rule: Require at least 2:1 reward to risk by default. Lower it for a setup only when the lower confidence bound of its logged hit rate supports the lower ratio.

rules.title: Debate outcome X10
rules.rule: Do not commit full size at an apparent bottom. Stage entries and wait for confirmation before the full position.

rules.title: Debate outcome X11
rules.rule: An extended or parabolic move alone is not a trigger to fade it. Wait for a confirmed reversal.

rules.title: Debate outcome X12
rules.rule: Neither blind mechanical trailing nor a never-touch rule: trail only to plan levels (structure, not ticks or ATR alone) and record each change.
